note: C-9 knight3d R-C9-59: whole-cycle solve, the plant constraint INSIDE the objective and the root eliminated by a linear solve rather than searched.

method.root: never a search variable. Given a cycle of joint angles, the root trajectory is recovered by a weighted linear least squares from the stance pins (root_y[i] + contact_y + D*phase = W_foot), ground contact (root_z[i] + contact_z = 0), a circular smoothness term that carries the root through flight frames, and a zero-mean term that keeps the figure centred. 14 unknowns, solved exactly, every objective evaluation.
method.slip_in_the_objective: the residual of that solve IS the slip and is added to the cost, so the optimiser is pushed toward angles whose pins are mutually consistent.
method.periodicity: each joint channel is a truncated Fourier series in cycle phase, so frame N IS frame 0 and the world has advanced exactly one stride by construction. Nothing is stitched at the loop point.
method.schedule: coarse to fine in harmonics (1, 2, 3), warm-started from the per-frame fit via FFT.
method.silhouette: fit runs on the analytic hull solids (37 ms per 12-frame evaluation after pre-hulling once); 05_verify measured those agreeing with the atlas mesh at 0.980 IoU. Shipped frames are rendered from the mesh.

walk_stance_experiment.question: is the walk's slip a weighting choice or a kinematic limit?
walk_stance_experiment.finding: weighting the slip 6x harder moved it only 86.8 -> 74.3 mm and cost IoU, so it was NOT a tuning choice. Cutting the double-support window from 52 % to 42 % collapsed it to 1.38 mm at the SAME IoU (0.6406 vs 0.6404). The walk's slip was the stance fraction being incompatible with the stride the cadence demands -- which is the Froude number measured at M-b saying the same thing: at 247 px/s this figure is kinematically jogging (v^2/gL = 1.12, transition is 0.5), and a jog has little double support.

sprites: out/sprites_fit/{walk,run}/E/ -- the procedural out/sprites/ was left untouched for the Astra paint-over.
